vbt-p03-v25.sanskrit_cite: maruto 'ntar bahir vāpi viyadyugmānivartanāt | bhairavyā bhairavasyettham bhairavi vyajyate vapuḥ

vbt-p03-v26.plain_english: Neither should it go nor enter, the wind-formed power when it blossoms; by thoughtlessness in the middle — by her, Bhairava-formness.
vbt-p03-v26.sanskrit_cite: na vrajen na viśec chaktir marudrūpā vikāsite | nirvikalpatayā madhye tayā bhairavarūpatā

vbt-p03-v27.plain_english: Whether kumbhaka-held, or exhaled, or inhaled — when it may be so: at its end this is called calm; by power, calm shines forth.
vbt-p03-v27.sanskrit_cite: kumbhitā recitā vāpi pūritā vā yadā bhavet | tadante śāntanāmāsau śaktyā śāntaḥ prakāśate

vbt-p03-v28.plain_english: From the root, ray-shining; from the subtle, the subtler-natured — contemplate her at the twelve's end, calming down: Bhairava's rise.
vbt-p03-v28.sanskrit_cite: āmūlāt kiraṇābhāsāṃ sūkṣmāt sūkṣmatarātmikam | cintayet tāṃ dviṣaṭkānte śyāmyantīm bhairavodayaḥ

vbt-p03-v29.plain_english: Rising up, lightning-formed, wheel by wheel, step by step; upward to three fists — until, then at the end, the great rise.
vbt-p03-v29.sanskrit_cite: udgacchantīṃ taḍitrūpām praticakraṃ kramāt kramam | ūrdhvaṃ muṣṭitrayaṃ yāvat tāvad ante mahodayaḥ

vbt-p03-v30.plain_english: Twelvefold course rightly, divided by twelve letters; through gross, subtle, supreme standing — freed, freed at last: Śiva.
vbt-p03-v30.sanskrit_cite: kramadvādaśakaṃ samyag dvādaśākṣarabheditam | sthūlasūkṣmaparasthityā muktvā muktvāntataḥ śivaḥ

vbt-p04-v31.plain_english: By that quick filling, to the crown's end broken through, by the brow-toss bridge: thought-free mind made — above all, all go forth.
vbt-p04-v31.sanskrit_cite: tayāpūryāśu mūrdhāntaṃ bhaṅktvā bhrūkṣepasetunā | nirvikalpaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā sarvordhve sarvagodgamaḥ

vbt-p04-v32.plain_english: With peacock feathers, with varied forms, with circles, in the five-void: of the meditating one, in the unsurpassed void, entry in the heart may be.
vbt-p04-v32.sanskrit_cite: śikhipakṣaiś citrarūpair ma.ṅdalaiḥ śūnyapañcakam | dhyāyato 'nuttare śūnye praveśo hṛdaye bhavet

vbt-p04-v33.plain_english: By just such course — wherever thought: in void, on the wall, on the supreme, on the vessel, self dissolved — the boon-giving.
vbt-p04-v33.sanskrit_cite: īdṛśena krameṇaiva yatra kutrāpi cintanā | śūnye kuḍye pare pātre svayaṃ līnā varapradā

vbt-p04-v34.plain_english: Inside the skull, mind placed; standing with eyes half closed: in order, from the mind's firmness, mark the to-be-marked — the highest.
vbt-p04-v34.sanskrit_cite: kapālāntar mano nyasya tiṣṭhan mīlitalocanaḥ | krameṇa manaso dārḍhyāt lakṣayet laṣyam uttamam

vbt-p04-v35.plain_english: Middle channel, standing in the middle, like a lotus-fiber; by the meditated inner sky, O Goddess — by that, god shines forth.
vbt-p04-v35.sanskrit_cite: madhyanāḍī madhyasaṃsthā bisasūtrābharūpayā | dhyātāntarvyomayā devyā tayā devaḥ prakāśate

vbt-p04-v36.plain_english: By the hand-blocked gaze-weapon, from the brow's splitting, from the door's blocking; when seen in the drop, in order, when dissolved — in that middle, the supreme standing.
vbt-p04-v36.sanskrit_cite: kararuddhadṛgastreṇa bhrūbhedād dvārarodhanāt | dṛṣṭe bindau kramāl līne tanmadhye paramā sthitiḥ

vbt-p04-v37.plain_english: The mark of subtle fire born of dwelling-inner-churn — the drop at the crest's end, in the heart, at dissolution's end: for the meditating one, dissolving.
vbt-p04-v37.sanskrit_cite: dhāmāntaḥkṣobhasambhūtasūkṣmāgnitilakākṛtim | binduṃ śikhānte hṛdaye layānte dhyāyato layaḥ

vbt-p04-v38.plain_english: In the unstruck, in the vessel-ear, in the broken sound, in the river's rushing; bathed in word-brahman, the supreme brahman is attained.
vbt-p04-v38.sanskrit_cite: anāhate pātrakarṇe 'bhagnaśabde sariddrute | śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ param brahmādhigacchati

vbt-p04-v39.plain_english: From the prolonged utterance of oṃ and the rest, at the prolonged end, from contemplating void: by void, by supreme power — to voidness she goes, O Bhairavī.
vbt-p04-v39.sanskrit_cite: praṇavādisamuccārāt plutānte śūnyabhāvānāt | śūnyayā parayā śaktyā śūnyatām eti bhairavi

vbt-p04-v40.plain_english: Of any letter whatsoever, the beginning and end should be contemplated: by void, become void, that man becomes void-formed.
vbt-p04-v40.sanskrit_cite: yasya kasyāpi varṇasya pūrvāntāv anubhāvayet | śūnyayā śūnyabhūto 'sau śūnyākāraḥ pumān bhavet

vbt-p05-v41.plain_english: In stringed instruments and the like, in the long tones of ordered resonance: with undivided mind at the limit, the body may become the supreme sky.
vbt-p05-v41.sanskrit_cite: tantryādivādyaśabdeṣu dīrgheṣu kramasaṃsthiteḥ | ananyacetāḥ pratyante paravyomavapur bhavet

vbt-p05-v42.plain_english: Of the body-mantra of all, by the gross-letter course — ending in moon-drop-sound: from void uttering, one may become Śiva.
vbt-p05-v42.sanskrit_cite: pi.ṅdamantrasya sarvasya sthūlavarṇakrameṇa tu | ardhendubindunādāntaḥ śūnyoccārād bhavec chivaḥ

vbt-p05-v43.plain_english: In one's own body, all directions at once should be contemplated as sky; with undirected mind — of him, sky proceeds everywhere.
vbt-p05-v43.sanskrit_cite: nijadehe sarvadikkaṃ yugapad bhāvayed viyat | nirvikalpamanās tasya viyat sarvam pravartate

vbt-p05-v44.plain_english: The back-void and the root-void at once should be contemplated, and whoever: by the body-disregarding power, void-minded he may be.
vbt-p05-v44.sanskrit_cite: pṛṣṭaśūnyaṃ mūlaśūnyaṃ yugapad bhāvayec ca yaḥ | śarīranirapekṣiṇyā śaktyā śūnyamanā bhavet

vbt-p05-v45.plain_english: Back-void, root-void, heart-void should be contemplated steady: at once, from thoughtlessness — thoughtless-rising follows.
vbt-p05-v45.sanskrit_cite: pṛṣṭaśūnyaṃ mūlaśūnyaṃ hṛcchūnyam bhāvayet sthiram | yugapan nirvikalpatvān nirvikalpodayas tataḥ

vbt-p05-v46.plain_english: In a place of the body, voidness indeed — for a mere moment should be envisioned: thoughtless, thoughtless, sharing thoughtless nature.
vbt-p05-v46.sanskrit_cite: tanūdeśe śūnyataiva kṣaṇamātraṃ vibhāvayet | nirvikalpaṃ nirvikalpo nirvikalpasvarūpabhāk

vbt-p05-v47.plain_english: All gone in the body-stuff, pervaded by sky, O deer-eyed one: should be envisioned then — of him, the contemplation may grow steady.
vbt-p05-v47.sanskrit_cite: sarvaṃ dehagataṃ dravyaṃ viyadvyāptaṃ mṛgekṣaṇe | vibhāvayet tatas tasya bhāvanā sā sthirā bhavet

vbt-p05-v48.plain_english: Inside the body, the skin-division should be thought through as a wall: nothing inside it — for the meditating one, the one beyond the meditated's share may be.
vbt-p05-v48.sanskrit_cite: dehāntare tvagvibhāgam bhittibhūtaṃ vicintayet | na kiṃcid antare tasya dhyāyann adhyeyabhāg bhavet

vbt-p05-v49.plain_english: In the heart-sky, eyes hidden, gone to the middle of the lotus-casket: with undivided mind, O fortunate one — supreme fortune may be won.
vbt-p05-v49.sanskrit_cite: hṛdyākāśe nilīnākṣaḥ padmasampuṭamadhyagaḥ | ananyacetāḥ subhage paraṃ saubhāgyam āpnuyāt

vbt-p05-v50.plain_english: From all around one's own body, at the twelve's end, from mind-dissolving: of firm-minded made firm, the reality-mark proceeds.
vbt-p05-v50.sanskrit_cite: sarvataḥ svaśarīrasya dvādaśānte manolayāt | dṛḍhabuddher dṛḍhībhūtaṃ tattvalakṣyam pravartate

vbt-p06-v51.plain_english: Just so, where there — at the twelve's end, the mind should be cast: moment by moment, of wasted turning, the strangeness drops away in days.
vbt-p06-v51.sanskrit_cite: yathā tathā yatra tatra dvādaśānte manaḥ kṣipet || pratikṣaṇaṃ kṣīṇavṛtter vailakṣaṇyaṃ dinair bhavet

vbt-p06-v52.plain_english: By the time-fire, arisen from the time-place — one's own city should be thought burnt; at the end, calm-shining, then it may be.
vbt-p06-v52.sanskrit_cite: kālāgninā kālapadād utthitena svakam puram | pluṣṭam vicintayed ante śāntābhāsas tadā bhavet

vbt-p06-v53.plain_english: Thus, indeed, the whole world burnt — having meditated, away from fancy: in the non-other mind of the man, manliness supreme may be.
vbt-p06-v53.sanskrit_cite: evam eva jagat sarvaṃ dagdhaṃ dhyātvā vikalpataḥ | ananyacetasaḥ puṃsaḥ pumbhāvaḥ paramo bhavet

vbt-p06-v54.plain_english: In one's own body, the world's or even the minute-minuter things and realities — their abiding contemplated at the end, the supreme is manifested.
vbt-p06-v54.sanskrit_cite: svadehe jagato vāpi sūkṣmasūkṣmatarāṇi ca | tattvāni yāni nilayaṃ dhyātvānte vyajyate parā

vbt-p06-v55.plain_english: The thin and weak power, meditated at the twelve's range: having entered, meditating in the heart — freed, freedom may be won.
vbt-p06-v55.sanskrit_cite: pināṃ ca durbalāṃ śaktiṃ dhyātvā dvādaśagocare | praviśya hṛdaye dhyāyan muktaḥ svātantryam āpnuyāt

vbt-p06-v56.plain_english: The world-course and the rest formed, in order, all: through gross, subtle, supreme standing — as long as, at the end, mind-dissolves.
vbt-p06-v56.sanskrit_cite: bhuvanādhvādirūpeṇa cintayet kramaśo 'khilam | sthūlasūkṣmaparasthityā yāvad ante manolayaḥ

vbt-p06-v57.plain_english: Of this, of all, of the world — at the ends everywhere; by path-procedure, Śiva-reality meditated: the great rise.
vbt-p06-v57.sanskrit_cite: asya sarvasya viśvasya paryanteṣu samantataḥ | adhvaprakriyayā tattvaṃ śaivaṃ dhyatvā mahodayaḥ

vbt-p06-v58.plain_english: The universe, this, O great Goddess, void-become should be thought; right there and mind merged — then, of that, the vessel of merging.
vbt-p06-v58.sanskrit_cite: viśvam etan mahādevi śūnyabhūtaṃ vicintayet | tatraiva ca mano līnaṃ tatas tallayabhājanam

vbt-p06-v59.plain_english: In a pot and such a vessel, the gaze — the wall left, cast well: at that dissolving, in that moment gone — made of that he may be.
vbt-p06-v59.sanskrit_cite: ghatādibhājane dṛṣṭim bhittis tyaktvā vinikṣipet | tallayaṃ tatkṣaṇād gatvā tallayāt tanmayo bhavet

vbt-p06-v60.plain_english: In a treeless mountain, a wall, such a place — the gaze should be cast well: when dissolved in mind, in that state, the wasting of turning is born.
vbt-p06-v60.sanskrit_cite: nirvṛkṣagiribhittyādideśe dṛṣṭiṃ vinikṣipet | vilīne mānase bhāve vṛttikṣiṇaḥ prajāyate

vbt-p07-v61.plain_english: Of the two, of the two states, in knowing having meditated — the middle should be resorted to: at once, with both left, in the middle reality shines forth.
vbt-p07-v61.sanskrit_cite: ubhayor bhāvayor jñāne dhyātvā madhyaṃ samāśrayet | yugapac ca dvayaṃ tyaktvā madhye tattvam prakāśate

vbt-p07-v62.plain_english: When the state is abandoned, the restrained consciousness does not go to any other state: then, in that middle-being, contemplation expands exceedingly.
vbt-p07-v62.sanskrit_cite: bhāve tyakte niruddhā cin naiva bhāvāntaraṃ vrajet | tadā tanmadhyabhāvena vikasatyati bhāvanā

vbt-p07-v63.plain_english: All body consciousness-made — or the world indeed, fancy fully: at once, by undivided mind, the supreme rise.
vbt-p07-v63.sanskrit_cite: sarvaṃ dehaṃ cinmayaṃ hi jagad vā paribhāvayet | yugapan nirvikalpena manasā paramodayaḥ

vbt-p07-v64.plain_english: Of the two winds, from their clashing — inside or outside, at the limit: the yogin, of the rising of evenness-knowing, becomes the vessel of offering.
vbt-p07-v64.sanskrit_cite: vāyudvayasya saṃghaṭṭād antar vā bahir antataḥ | yogī samatvavijñānasamudgamanabhājanam

vbt-p07-v65.plain_english: All world, or one's own body, filled with one's own bliss should be remembered: at once with one's own nectar indeed — full of supreme bliss he may be.
vbt-p07-v65.sanskrit_cite: sarvaṃ jagat svadehaṃ vā svānandabharitaṃ smaret | yugapat svāmṛtenaiva parānandamayo bhavet

vbt-p07-v66.plain_english: By trick, by application — at once indeed, O deer-eyed one: great bliss manifests, by which reality shines forth.
vbt-p07-v66.sanskrit_cite: kuhanena prayogeṇa sadya eva mṛgekṣaṇe | samudeti mahānando yena tattvaṃ prakāśate

vbt-p07-v67.plain_english: By binding all the channels, by the up-going breath-power, slowly: at the crawling-ant's moment, supreme happiness spreads forth.
vbt-p07-v67.sanskrit_cite: sarvasrotonibandhena prāṇaśaktyordhvayā śanaiḥ | pipīlasparśavelāyām prathate paramaṃ sukham

vbt-p07-v68.plain_english: Between fire and poison, in the middle — the mind, happiness-made, should be cast: merely wind-filled, or yoked by remembrance-bliss.
vbt-p07-v68.sanskrit_cite: vahner viṣasya madhye tu cittaṃ sukhamayaṃ kṣipet | kevalaṃ vāyupūrṇaṃ vā smarānandena yujyate

vbt-p07-v69.plain_english: Agitated by union, shaking, at the end of power-penetration: whatever happiness of brahman-reality — that happiness, self-told, is told.
vbt-p07-v69.sanskrit_cite: śaktisaṃgamasaṃkṣubdhaśaktyāveśāvasānikam | yat sukham brahmatattvasya tat sukhaṃ svākyam ucyate

vbt-p07-v70.plain_english: By licking, churning, the pounding apexes — of woman-bliss from fullness, from memory: even in power's absence, O Goddess of gods, the bliss-flood may be.
vbt-p07-v70.sanskrit_cite: lehanāmanthanākoṭaiḥ strīsukhasya bharāt smṛteḥ | śaktyabhāve 'pi deveśi bhaved ānandasamplavaḥ

vbt-p08-v71.plain_english: In joy, in greatness, when it is won — seen or a kinsman long after: bliss risen, having meditated it, dissolved in that — of that mind may be.
vbt-p08-v71.sanskrit_cite: ānande mahati prāpte dṛṣṭe vā bāndhave cirāt | ānandam udgataṃ dhyātvā tallayas tanmanā bhavet

vbt-p08-v72.plain_english: From eating and drinking, the swelling of joy, bliss-blooming: should be fancied the filled state — great bliss then may be.
vbt-p08-v72.sanskrit_cite: jagdhipānakṛtollāsarasānandavijṛmbhaṇāt | bhāvayed bharitāvasthāṃ mahānandas tato bhavet

vbt-p08-v73.plain_english: From tasting objects such as song — happiness not shared, one-selfness: of the yogin, by absorbedness, mounted in mind — in that selfness.

vbt-p08-v74.plain_english: Wherever the mind is content, right there the mind should be held: there, there — the own-form of supreme bliss proceeds forth.
vbt-p08-v74.sanskrit_cite: yatra yatra manas tuṣṭir manas tatraiva dhārayet | tatra tatra parānandasvārūpaṃ sampravartate

vbt-p08-v75.plain_english: In the not-yet-come, in sleep, when the outer range has perished: that state, to be gone to by mind — the supreme Goddess shines forth.
vbt-p08-v75.sanskrit_cite: anāgatāyāṃ nidrāyām praṇaṣṭe bāhyagocare | sāvasthā manasā gamyā parā devī prakāśate

vbt-p08-v76.plain_english: By the brilliance of sun, lamp and such, in the sky made dappled: gaze fixed right there — one's own self-form shines forth.
vbt-p08-v76.sanskrit_cite: tejasā sūryadīpāder ākāśe śabalīkṛte | dṛṣṭir niveśyā tatraiva svātmarūpam prakāśate

vbt-p08-v77.plain_english: By the skeleton, by the angry, by the licking Bhairavī, by the sky-going: at the gaze's time — the supreme attainment shines forth.
vbt-p08-v77.sanskrit_cite: karaṅkiṇyā krodhanayā bhairavyā lelihānayā | khecaryā dṛṣṭikāle ca parāvāptiḥ prakāśate

vbt-p08-v78.plain_english: On a soft seat, with one buttock, hands and feet unsupported placed: by that context — the supreme, full mind may be.
vbt-p08-v78.sanskrit_cite: mṛdvāsane sphijaikena hastapādau nirāśrayam | nidhāya tatprasaṅgena parā pūrṇā matir bhavet

vbt-p08-v79.plain_english: Having sat on the seat rightly, arms, two, made half-bent: in the armpit-sky, mind making — calm comes by that dissolving.
vbt-p08-v79.sanskrit_cite: upaviśyāsane samyag bāhū kṛtvārdhakuñcitau | kakṣavyomni manaḥ kurvan śamam āyāti tallayāt

vbt-p08-v80.plain_english: Of gross-formed state, fixed gaze cast down, and quickly: unsupported mind made — Śiva one may go to.
vbt-p08-v80.sanskrit_cite: sthūlarūpasya bhāvasya stabdhāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ nipātya ca | acireṇa nirādhāraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā śivaṃ vrajet

vbt-p09-v81.plain_english: On the middle tongue, in the opened mouth, in the middle — awareness cast: the h-uttering made by mind, then in calm it dissolves.
vbt-p09-v81.sanskrit_cite: madhyajihve sphāritāsye madhye nikṣipya cetanām | hoccāraṃ manasā kurvaṃs tataḥ śānte pralīyate

vbt-p09-v82.plain_english: On seat, on bed, having stood — unsupported, envisioning one's own body in mind: when mind wasted — in a moment, wasted-impurity may be.
vbt-p09-v82.sanskrit_cite: āsane śayane sthitvā nirādhāraṃ vibhāvayan | svadehaṃ manasi kṣiṇe kṣaṇāt kṣīṇāśayo bhavet

vbt-p09-v83.plain_english: On a moving seat, standing now — slowly, or by the body's moving: in the calmed mind, in that state, O Goddess, the divine flood may be won.
vbt-p09-v83.sanskrit_cite: calāsane sthitasyātha śanair vā dehacālanāt | praśānte mānase bhāve devi divyaugham āpnuyāt

vbt-p09-v84.plain_english: Sky, stainless, seeing — gaze made unbroken: stunned self at that moment, O Goddess, the Bhairava form may be won.
vbt-p09-v84.sanskrit_cite: ākāśaṃ vimalam paśyan kṛtvā dṛṣṭiṃ nirantarām | stabdhātmā tatkṣaṇād devi bhairavaṃ vapur āpnuyāt

vbt-p09-v85.plain_english: Dissolved on the crown, sky all as Bhairava should be contemplated: that all — the Bhairava-form-blaze-reality may enter.
vbt-p09-v85.sanskrit_cite: līnaṃ mūrdhni viyat sarvam bhairavatvena bhāvayet | tat sarvam bhairavākāratejastattvaṃ samāviśet

vbt-p09-v86.plain_english: Something known — duality-giving, outer light, darkness again: the universe-form of Bhairava — having known, endless-light-bearing.
vbt-p09-v86.sanskrit_cite: kiñcij jñātaṃ dvaitadāyi bāhyālokas tamaḥ punaḥ | viśvādi bhairavaṃ rūpaṃ jñātvānantaprakāśabhṛt

vbt-p09-v87.plain_english: Thus indeed in bad night, on the dark fortnight's arrival, long: contemplating timira — Bhairava's form will come to.
vbt-p09-v87.sanskrit_cite: evam eva durniśāyāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣāgame ciram | taimiram bhāvayan rūpam bhairavaṃ rūpam eṣyati

vbt-p09-v88.plain_english: Thus indeed, having closed first the eyes, black lustre before: spread Bhairava's form, contemplating — made of that he may be.
vbt-p09-v88.sanskrit_cite: evam eva nimīlyādau netre kṛṣṇābham agrataḥ | prasārya bhairavaṃ rūpam bhāvayaṃs tanmayo bhavet

vbt-p09-v89.plain_english: Of whichever organ even — from its striking and its blocking: of one entered in the nondual, in void — there itself the self shines forth.
vbt-p09-v89.sanskrit_cite: yasya kasyendriyasyāpi vyāghātāc ca nirodhataḥ | praviṣṭasyādvaye śūnye tatraivātmā prakāśate

vbt-p09-v90.plain_english: No drop, no emission, and the a-syllable of muttering great: rises, O Goddess, suddenly — knowledge-flood, the highest Lord.
vbt-p09-v90.sanskrit_cite: abindum avisargaṃ ca akāraṃ japato mahān | udeti devi sahasā jñānaughaḥ parameśvaraḥ

vbt-p10-v91.plain_english: Of letter with emission — emission-ending awareness make: by supportless mind, eternal brahman may be touched.
vbt-p10-v91.sanskrit_cite: varṇasya savisargasya visargāntaṃ citiṃ kuru | nirādhāreṇa cittena spṛśed brahma sanātanam

vbt-p10-v92.plain_english: Sky-formed one's own self should be meditated, by directions uncovered: supportless awareness-power — own form will show it then.
vbt-p10-v92.sanskrit_cite: vyomākāraṃ svam ātmānaṃ dhyāyed digbhir anāvṛtam | nirāśrayā citiḥ śaktiḥ svarūpaṃ darśayet tadā

vbt-p10-v93.plain_english: Something, a limb, pierced first — with sharp needle and such, then: right there, awareness yoked — in Bhairava, spotless going.
vbt-p10-v93.sanskrit_cite: kiṃcid aṅgaṃ vibhidyādau tīkṣṇasūcyādinā tataḥ | tatraiva cetanāṃ yuktvā bhairave nirmalā gatiḥ

vbt-p10-v94.plain_english: Mind-and-the-rest, inner-making, is not inside me: think thus — by absence of fancies, fancies abandoned may be.
vbt-p10-v94.sanskrit_cite: cittādyantaḥkṛtir nāsti mamāntar bhāvayed iti | vikalpānām abhāvena vikalpair ujjhito bhavet

vbt-p10-v95.plain_english: Māyā, the deluding one, named: the counting of the parts stands; counting the such-and-such natures of realities — not separately may be.
vbt-p10-v95.sanskrit_cite: māyā vimohinī nāma kalāyāḥ kalanaṃ sthitam | ityādidharmaṃ tattvānāṃ kalayan na pṛthag bhavet

vbt-p10-v96.plain_english: Sudden desire arisen — having seen it, to calm should lead it: where it indeed arose, there right there it dissolves.
vbt-p10-v96.sanskrit_cite: jhagitīcchāṃ samutpannām avalokya śamaṃ nayet | yata eva samudbhūtā tatas tatraiva līyate

vbt-p10-v97.plain_english: When my desire is unarisen — knowing, or what — then I am indeed: truly He-I, thus become, in that dissolved, that-minded may be.
vbt-p10-v97.sanskrit_cite: yadā mamecchā notpannā jñānaṃ vā kas tadāsmi vai | tattvato =B9haṃ tathābhūtas tallīnas tanmanā bhavet

vbt-p10-v98.plain_english: In desire or in knowing, when arisen — mind should be set: self-mind, undivided-minded — then the seeing of reality's meaning.
vbt-p10-v98.sanskrit_cite: icchāyām athavā jñāne jāte cittaṃ niveśayet | ātmabuddhyānanyacetās tatas tattvārthadarśanam

vbt-p10-v99.plain_english: Causeless may be the knowing, supportless, error-natured: truly not anyone's — thus becoming Śiva, O dear.
vbt-p10-v99.sanskrit_cite: nirnimittam bhavej jñānaṃ nirādhāram bhramātmakam | tattvataḥ kasyacin naitad evambhāvī śivaḥ priye

vbt-p10-v100.plain_english: Consciousness-natured in all bodies — distinction there is nowhere: hence, made of that, contemplating all — the world-conquering person.
vbt-p10-v100.sanskrit_cite: ciddharmā sarvadeheṣu viśeṣo nāsti kutracit | ataś ca tanmayaṃ sarvam bhāvayan bhavajij janaḥ

vbt-p11-v101.plain_english: In the range of lust, anger, greed, delusion, pride and envy — intellect uncaused having been made, that reality remains.
vbt-p11-v101.sanskrit_cite: kāmakrodhalobhamohamadamātsaryagocare | buddhiṃ nistimitāṃ kṛtvā tat tattvam avaśiṣyate

vbt-p11-v102.plain_english: The world, Indra-net-made, cast — or picture-work-like; whirling, or the meditating one's all: and seeing — joy upsurges.
vbt-p11-v102.sanskrit_cite: indrajālamayaṃ viśvaṃ vyastaṃ vā citrakarmavat | bhramad vā dhyāyataḥ sarvam paśyataś ca sukhodgamaḥ

vbt-p11-v103.plain_english: Not into pain should the mind be cast, not into joy, nor scattered about: O Bhairavī — in the middle, what reality remains may be known.
vbt-p11-v103.sanskrit_cite: na cittaṃ nikṣiped duḥkhe na sukhe vā parikṣipet | bhairavi jñāyatāṃ madhye kiṃ tattvam avaśiṣyate

vbt-p11-v104.plain_english: Having left the own-body-standing, contemplating everywhere-I-am-thus: with firm mind, by a gaze not seeing elsewhere — happy may he be.
vbt-p11-v104.sanskrit_cite: vihāya nijadehasthaṃ sarvatrāsmīti bhāvayan | dṛḍhena manasā dṛṣṭyā nānyekṣiṇyā sukhī bhavet

vbt-p11-v105.plain_english: In a pot and such — whatever knowing; desire and such, or inside me: never all-pervading born — contemplating thus, all-going.
vbt-p11-v105.sanskrit_cite: ghaṭādau yac ca vijñānam icchādyaṃ vā mamāntare | naiva sarvagataṃ jātam bhāvayan iti sarvagaḥ

vbt-p11-v106.plain_english: Grasper-grasped awareness: common to all embodied; of yogins the distinction but — He is, in relation, carefulness.
vbt-p11-v106.sanskrit_cite: grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittiḥ sāmānyā sarvadehinām | yogināṃ tu viśeṣo =B9sti sambandhe sāvadhānatā

vbt-p11-v107.plain_english: Like self in another body — He even should perceive awareness: regard of one's own body having left, pervasive in days may he be.
vbt-p11-v107.sanskrit_cite: svavad anyaśarīre =B9pi saṃvittim anubhāvayet | apekṣāṃ svaśarīrasya tyaktvā vyāpī dinair bhavet

vbt-p11-v108.plain_english: Supportless mind having been made — thoughts should not be thought: then, in self-supreme-self — Bhairava, O deer-eyed one.
vbt-p11-v108.sanskrit_cite: nirādhāraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā vikalpān na vikalpayet | tadātmaparamātmatve bhairavo mṛgalocane

vbt-p11-v109.plain_english: All-knowing, all-doing, and pervasive, the highest Lord: he indeed I — Śiva-natured; hence from firmness, Śiva may one be.
vbt-p11-v109.sanskrit_cite: sarvajñaḥ sarvakartā ca vyāpakaḥ parameśvaraḥ | sa evāhaṃ śaivadharmā iti dārḍhyāc chivo bhavet

vbt-p11-v110.plain_english: Like the waves of water, the flame-plays of fire, the sun's light: of me indeed, of Bhairava — these world-plays, manifested.
vbt-p11-v110.sanskrit_cite: jalasyevormayo vahner jvālābhaṅgyaḥ prabhā raveḥ | mamaiva bhairavasyaitā viśvabhaṅgyo vibheditāḥ

vbt-p12-v111.plain_english: Having whirled, whirled — by the body swiftly, falling to earth: by the ceasing of agitation-power, the supreme state is born.
vbt-p12-v111.sanskrit_cite: bhrāntvā bhrāntvā śarīreṇa tvaritam bhuvi pātanāt | kṣobhaśaktivirāmeṇa parā saṃjāyate daśā

vbt-p12-v112.plain_english: On supports or by power, by knowing, or from mind-dissolving: born at power-penetration's end — the Bhairava form.
vbt-p12-v112.sanskrit_cite: ādhāreṣv athavā 'śaktyā 'jñānāc cittalayena vā | jātaśaktisamāveśakṣobhānte bhairavaṃ vapuḥ

vbt-p12-v113.plain_english: This tradition, O Goddess, hear — rightly I tell: even freedom is born at once, when the eyes are unwinkingly fixed.
vbt-p12-v113.sanskrit_cite: sampradāyam imam devi śṛṇu samyag vadāmy aham | kaivalyaṃ jāyate sadyo netrayoḥ stabdhamātrayoḥ

vbt-p12-v114.plain_english: Contraction of the ears having been made — at the lower gate likewise: unsmeared, unploughed, meditating, one may enter eternal brahman.
vbt-p12-v114.sanskrit_cite: saṃkocaṃ karṇayoḥ kṛtvā hy adhodvāre tathaiva ca | anackam ahalaṃ dhyāyan viśed brahma sanātanam

vbt-p12-v115.plain_english: At a well and such, a great pit — having stood above, from looking: of undivided mind rightly, at once mind-dissolving, plainly.
vbt-p12-v115.sanskrit_cite: kūpādike mahāgarte sthitvopari nirīkṣaṇāt | avikalpamateḥ samyak sadyas cittalayaḥ sphuṭam

vbt-p12-v116.plain_english: Wherever the mind goes — outside or inside, or even so: there, there Śiva-state — by pervasiveness: where would it go?
vbt-p12-v116.sanskrit_cite: yatra yatra mano yāti bāhye vābhyantare 'pi vā | tatra tatra śivāvāsthā vyāpakatvāt kva yāsyati

vbt-p12-v117.plain_english: Wherever by the eye's road, consciousness is manifested of the pervader: of him, from only-that-natured, from cit-dissolving — full-selfness.
vbt-p12-v117.sanskrit_cite: yatra yatrākṣamārgeṇa caitanyaṃ vyajyate vibhoḥ | tasya tanmātradharmitvāc cillayād bharitātmatā

vbt-p12-v118.plain_english: At hunger's end and such — in fear, in grief, in the abyss, or fled from battle; at curiosity-thirst's end: reality-being-full state.
vbt-p12-v118.sanskrit_cite: kṣutādyante bhaye śoke gahvare vā raṇād drute | kutūhalekṣudhādyante brahmasattāmayī daśā

vbt-p12-v119.plain_english: In things being remembered, when seen — in place, the mind should leave: one's own body unsupported made, the lord spreads forth.
vbt-p12-v119.sanskrit_cite: vastuṣu smaryamāṇeṣu dṛṣṭe deśe manas tyajet | svaśarīraṃ nirādhāraṃ kṛtvā prasarati prabhuḥ

vbt-p12-v120.plain_english: Anywhere, on a thing placed — slowly the gaze should withdraw: that knowing, mind-with — O Goddess, void-abode may it be.
vbt-p12-v120.sanskrit_cite: kvacid vastuni vinyasya śanair dṛṣṭiṃ nivartayet | taj jñānaṃ cittasahitaṃ devi śūnyālāyo bhavet

vbt-p13-v121.plain_english: From the excess of devotion, of the dispassionate one — as which the mind arises: she, power, Śaṅkara's — always should contemplate her; then Śiva.
vbt-p13-v121.sanskrit_cite: bhaktyudrekād viraktasya yādṛśī jāyate matiḥ | sā śaktiḥ śāṅkarī nityam bhavayet tāṃ tataḥ śivaḥ

vbt-p13-v122.plain_english: In things inside, being known — in all things, voidness: her indeed, by mind meditated — known even, becomes calm.
vbt-p13-v122.sanskrit_cite: vastvantare vedyamāne sarvavastuṣu śūnyatā | tām eva manasā dhyātvā vidito 'pi praśāmyati

vbt-p13-v123.plain_english: By slightly knowing which is remembered purity — that purity in Śambhu's view: not pure, nor impure therefore — thought-free, happy may he be.
vbt-p13-v123.sanskrit_cite: kiṃcijjñair yā smṛtā śuddhiḥ sā śuddhiḥ śambhudarśane | na śucir hy aśucis tasmān nirvikalpaḥ sukhī bhavet

vbt-p13-v124.plain_english: Everywhere Bhairava's state — even in common things, the object: not apart from that higher thus — the nondual going.
vbt-p13-v124.sanskrit_cite: sarvatra bhairavo bhāvaḥ sāmānyeṣv api gocaraḥ | na ca tadvyatirekteṇa paro 'stīty advayā gatiḥ

vbt-p13-v125.plain_english: Same in enemy and in friend; same in honor and dishonor: of brahman's fullness — thus having known, happy may he be.
vbt-p13-v125.sanskrit_cite: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca samo mānāvamānayoḥ || brahmaṇaḥ paripūrṇatvāt iti jñātvā sukhī bhavet

vbt-p13-v126.plain_english: Not hatred should one contemplate anywhere, not passion anywhere: free of passion and hatred — in the middle, brahman glides forth.
vbt-p13-v126.sanskrit_cite: na dveṣam bhāvayet kvāpi na rāgam bhāvayet kvacit | rāgadveṣavinirmuktau madhye brahma prasarpati

vbt-p13-v127.plain_english: Whatever unknowable, whatever ungraspable, whatever void, whatever gone to nonbeing: that all as Bhairava to be contemplated — at that end, awakening arises.
vbt-p13-v127.sanskrit_cite: yad avedyaṃ yad agrāhyaṃ yac chūnyaṃ yad abhāvagam | tat sarvam bhairavam bhāvyaṃ tadante bodhasambhavaḥ

vbt-p13-v128.plain_english: In the eternal, in the supportless, in the void, in the pervasive, free of counting: mind made in the outer sky — into the skyless should enter.
vbt-p13-v128.sanskrit_cite: nitye nirāśraye śūnye vyāpake kalanojjhite | bāhyākāśe manaḥ kṛtvā nirākāśaṃ samāviśet

vbt-p13-v129.plain_english: Wherever the mind goes — that, that by that very thing at that moment: having left non-standing — waveless then may it be.
vbt-p13-v129.sanskrit_cite: yatra yatra mano yāti tat tat tenaiva tatkṣaṇam | parityajyānavasthityā nistaraṅgas tato bhavet

vbt-p13-v130.plain_english: By fear all makes resound — giving all, pervasive in wholeness: hence of Bhairava's word, from constant uttering — Śiva.
vbt-p13-v130.sanskrit_cite: bhayā sarvaṃ ravayati sarvado vyāpako 'khile | iti bhairavaśabdasya santatoccāraṇāc chivaḥ

vbt-p14-v131.plain_english: 'I', 'mine', 'this' and such — from coming to conviction: in supportless mind it goes — from that meditation's impulse, calm.
vbt-p14-v131.sanskrit_cite: ahaṃ mamedam ityādi pratipattiprasaṅgataḥ | nirādhāre mano yāti taddhyānapreraṇāc chamī

vbt-p14-v132.plain_english: Eternal, all-pervading, supportless, pervasive, and lord of all: words moment by moment meditated — aim done according to meaning.
vbt-p14-v132.sanskrit_cite: nityo vibhur nirādhāro vyāpakaś cākhilādhipaḥ | śabdān pratikṣaṇaṃ dhyāyan kṛtārtho 'rthānurūpataḥ

vbt-p14-v133.plain_english: Non-reality, Indra-net-shine — this all standing: what reality of the Indra-net? Thus from firmness, calm may go.
vbt-p14-v133.sanskrit_cite: atattvam indrajālābham idaṃ sarvam avasthitam | kiṃ tattvam indrajālasya iti dārḍhyāc chamaṃ vrajet

vbt-p14-v134.plain_english: Of self, unwavering — where knowing, where action? Knowing-dependent outer states: hence void, this world.
vbt-p14-v134.sanskrit_cite: ātmano nirvikārasya kva jñānaṃ kva ca vā kriyā | jñānāyattā bahirbhāvā ataḥ śūnyam idaṃ jagat

vbt-p14-v135.plain_english: Not of me bondage, not freedom — of the frightened, these terrors: this reflection of the intellect in waters, like the sun's.
vbt-p14-v135.sanskrit_cite: na me bandho na mokṣo me bhītasyaitā vibhīṣikāḥ | pratibimbam idam buddher jaleṣv iva vivasvataḥ

vbt-p14-v136.plain_english: Sense-doored, all — meeting pleasure, pain and such: senses thus having left, self-abiding — in one's own self one abides.
vbt-p14-v136.sanskrit_cite: indriyadvārakaṃ sarvaṃ sukhaduḥkhādisaṃgamam | itīndriyāṇi saṃtyajya svasthaḥ svātmani vartate

vbt-p14-v137.plain_english: Knowing-lighting all — by all self lighting: one, from one-natureness — knowing, knowable, is envisioned.
vbt-p14-v137.sanskrit_cite: jñānaprakāśakaṃ sarvaṃ sarveṇātmā prakāśakaḥ | ekam ekasvabhāvatvāt jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ vibhāvyate

vbt-p14-v138.plain_english: Mental, consciousness, power, self, and mind — the fourfold: when, O dear, fully wasted — then that Bhairava form.
vbt-p14-v138.sanskrit_cite: mānasaṃ cetanā śaktir ātmā ceti catuṣṭayam | yadā priye parikṣīṇaṃ tadā tad bhairavaṃ vapuḥ

vbt-p14-v139.plain_english: Of waveless teachings, a hundred told in brief; twelve-plus — O Goddess, which having known, the knowing-knower person.
vbt-p14-v139.sanskrit_cite: nistaraṅgopadeśānāṃ śatam uktaṃ samāsataḥ | dvādaśābhyadhikaṃ devi yaj jñātvā jñānavij janaḥ

vbt-p14-v140.plain_english: Here and in one, yoked — he becomes Bhairava himself: by speech does deeds — curse-and-favor making.
vbt-p14-v140.sanskrit_cite: atra caikatame yukto jāyate bhairavaḥ svayam | vācā karoti karmāṇi śāpānugrahakārakaḥ

vbt-p15-v141.plain_english: Ageless deathlessness he attains, endowed with atom-and-the-rest qualities: of the yoginīs dear one, O Goddess — the lord who gathers all.
vbt-p15-v141.sanskrit_cite: ajarāmaratām eti so 'ṇimādiguṇānvitaḥ | yoginīnām priyo devi sarvamelāpakādhipaḥ

vbt-p15-v142.plain_english: Living even, freed he; acting even — not smeared: this body, if of supreme and great lord, O god.
vbt-p15-v142.sanskrit_cite: jīvann api vimukto 'sau kurvann api na lipyate | idaṃ yadi vapur deva parāyāś ca maheśvara

vbt-p15-v143.plain_english: In the state thus told — who mutters, who does muting, and who meditates: who is worshipped, O great lord, and who is pleased?
vbt-p15-v143.sanskrit_cite: evamuktavyavasthāyāṃ japyate ko japaś ca kaḥ | dhyāyate ko mahānātha pūjyate kaś ca tṛpyati

vbt-p15-v144.plain_english: Who is offered oblation, or the sacrifice — whose, and what, and how? This procedure here is outer, in gross things indeed, O deer-eyed one.
vbt-p15-v144.sanskrit_cite: hūyate kasya vā homo yāgaḥ kasya ca kiṃ katham | eṣātra prakriyā bāhyā sthūleṣv eva mṛgekṣaṇe

vbt-p15-v145.plain_english: Again, again in the supreme state — which contemplation is contemplated indeed: muting there itself — self-sound, mantra-natured — such the to-be-muted.
vbt-p15-v145.sanskrit_cite: bhūyo bhūyaḥ pare bhāve bhāvanā bhāvyate hi yā | japaḥ so 'tra svayaṃ nādo mantrātmā japya īdṛśaḥ

vbt-p15-v146.plain_english: Meditation indeed: unmoving intellect, formless, supportless; not meditation — the imagining of body, eye, mouth, hand and such.
vbt-p15-v146.sanskrit_cite: dhyānaṃ hi niścalā buddhir nirākārā nirāśrayā | na tu dhyānaṃ śarīrākṣimukhahastādikalpanā

vbt-p15-v147.plain_english: Worship is named not by flowers and such — which mind is made firm: in the undifferentiated great sky, that worship indeed from care, dissolving.
vbt-p15-v147.sanskrit_cite: pūjā nāma na puṣpādyair yā matiḥ kriyate dṛḍhā | nirvikalpe mahāvyomni sā pūjā hy ādarāl layaḥ

vbt-p15-v148.plain_english: Here in one or another yoking-standing, when it may arise from day to day: full-formed state — right here contentment, utter fullness.
vbt-p15-v148.sanskrit_cite: atraikatamayuktisthe yotpadyeta dinād dinam | bharitākāratā sātra tṛptir atyantapūrṇatā

vbt-p15-v149.plain_english: In the great void-abode, in the fire — sense-objects and such: offered by mind, with all oblation, with the awareness-ladle.
vbt-p15-v149.sanskrit_cite: mahāśūnyālaye vahnau bhūtākṣaviṣayādikam | hūyate manasā sārdhaṃ sa homaś cetanāsrucā

vbt-p15-v150.plain_english: The sacrifice here, O highest lady — contentment, bliss-marked: from wasting all sins, from protecting all — O mountain's daughter.
vbt-p15-v150.sanskrit_cite: yāgo 'tra parameśāni tuṣṭir ānandalakṣaṇā | kṣapaṇāt sarvapāpānāṃ trāṇāt sarvasya pārvati

vbt-p16-v151.plain_english: Rudra-power-penetration: that field — contemplation supreme: otherwise of it, of reality — what worship, and which is pleased?
vbt-p16-v151.sanskrit_cite: rudraśaktisamāveśas tat kṣetram bhāvanā parā | anyathā tasya tattvasya kā pūjā kāś ca tṛpyati

vbt-p16-v152.plain_english: Free-bliss-consciousness-mere-essence — one's own self everywhere: entering in that form — one's own self's bath, declared.
vbt-p16-v152.sanskrit_cite: svatantrānandacinmātrasāraḥ svātmā hi sarvataḥ | āveśanaṃ tatsvarūpe svātmanaḥ snānam īritam

vbt-p16-v153.plain_english: By which indeed is one worshipped, with materials pleased — or higher-lower: who indeed the worshipper — all he, the very one: where the worship?
vbt-p16-v153.sanskrit_cite: yair eva pūjyate dravyais tarpyate vā parāparaḥ | yaś caiva pūjakaḥ sarvaḥ sa evaikaḥ kva pūjanam

vbt-p16-v154.plain_english: Breath may go, life may enter — by will, crooked-formed: long-formed she, the great goddess — other field, higher-lower.
vbt-p16-v154.sanskrit_cite: vrajet prāṇo viśej jīva icchayā kuṭilākṛtiḥ | dīrghātmā sā mahādevī parakṣetram parāparā

vbt-p16-v155.plain_english: In this walking along, standing in the great-bliss-made path: by her, by the goddess entered — supreme Bhairava may attain.
vbt-p16-v155.sanskrit_cite: asyām anucaran tiṣṭhan mahānandamaye 'dhvare | tayā devyā samāviṣṭaḥ param bhairavam āpnuyāt

vbt-p16-v156.plain_english: Six hundreds by day, by night a thousand twenty-one: the goddess's muting declared — easy, hard for the dull.
vbt-p16-v156.sanskrit_cite: ṣaṭśatāni divā rātrau sahasrāṇyekaviṃśatiḥ | japo devyāḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ sulabho durlabho jaḍaiḥ

vbt-p16-v157.plain_english: Thus this told, O Goddess — supreme nectar, the highest: this and never to be shown of anyone, but ever.
vbt-p16-v157.sanskrit_cite: ity etat kathitaṃ devi paramāmṛtam uttamam | etac ca naiva kasyāpi prakāśyaṃ tu kadācana

vbt-p16-v158.plain_english: To another pupil, to the base, to the cruel, the non-devoted — of the guru's feet: but of thought-free-minded, of heroes, of lofty-souled.
vbt-p16-v158.sanskrit_cite: paraśiṣye khale krūre abhakte gurupādayoḥ | nirvikalpamatīnāṃ tu vīrāṇām unnatātmanām

vbt-p16-v159.plain_english: To the devoted, of the guru's company — to be given without hesitation: village, kingdom, town, country, son, wife, family.
vbt-p16-v159.sanskrit_cite: bhaktānāṃ guruvargasya dātavyaṃ nirviśaṅkayā | grāmo rājyam puraṃ deśaḥ putradārakuṭumbakam

vbt-p16-v160.plain_english: All this having left — this to be grasped, O deer-eyed one: what with these unsteady, O Goddess? This steady, supreme wealth; lives even to be given — the supreme nectar not to be given.
vbt-p16-v160.sanskrit_cite: sarvam etat parityajya grāhyam etan mṛgekṣaṇe | kim ebhir asthirair devi sthiram param idaṃ dhanam | prāṇā api pradātavyā na deyaṃ paramāmṛtam

vbt-p17-v161.plain_english: God of gods, great god — fully content am I, Śaṅkara: the essence of the Rudrayāmala-tantra, today held.
vbt-p17-v161.sanskrit_cite: devadeva māhadeva paritṛptāsmi śaṅkara | rudrayāmalatantrasya sāram adyāvadhāritam

vbt-p17-v162.plain_english: Of all the power-divisions, the heart known today, and: having spoken thus, delighted, the goddess on the neck — clung to Śiva's.
vbt-p17-v162.sanskrit_cite: sarvaśaktiprabhedānāṃ hṛdayaṃ jñātam adya ca | ity uktvānanditā devi ka.ṅthe lagnā śivasya tu

essence: Heard: all, Rudrayāmala-born, Trika division by essence.
Even now doubt not dispelled: what form in truth?
Nine-self, Bhairava-form, three-head, power-triad: which?
Nāda-drop, moon-crescent, wheel-unsmeared, power-formed: what?
Higher-lower whole: if higher thus, higher-ness contradicts.
Not by letter, not by body: higher-ness is partlessness.
Grace cuts the doubt: what was asked is the tantra's essence.
Most hidden, yet told: the whole form of Bhairava.
Known by unsubstantialness: Indra-net, māyā-dream, Gandharva-city.
Described for meditation's sake, for fancy-struck men only.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta with jijñāsā (wonder sharpened into seeking)
rasa.justification: Wonder at a text that collapses every offered form, answered by the Goddess's insistence: the doubt itself is the essence-question, so desire-to-know is the verse's drive, not decoration.

sections.SUMMARY: She has heard all, Rudrayāmala-born, Trika by essence — and doubts anyway: what form is it truly? Nine-self, three-head, power-triad, nāda-drop, wheel: each offering collapses — higher-ness is partlessness, not letter or body. Grace cuts the doubt, for what she asked is the tantra's essence; the most hidden will be told whole, known only as unsubstantial — net, dream, mirage-city — and described merely for fancy-struck minds.
sections.FUNCTION: Opens the dialogue as a genuine doubt-question whose answers dissolve their own objects.
sections.KEY TERMS: rudrayāmala (arisen from the union — Bhairavī speaks); trika-bheda (Trika corpus whole); sārāt sāravibhāgaśaḥ (essence by essence — ever more distilled); svasaṃvedana (self-feeling — planted for p02); saṃśaya (doubt as essence-engine).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: The doubt (v2) opens a question the denials (p02) and the telling (v8-10) answer; no rite yet — pure interrogation.
sections.BOUNDARY: No practice is given here; the forms offered are questions, not techniques — the dhāraṇās belong to later sections.
sections.EXPLANATION: The frame dialogue: a goddess who already possesses the teaching still asks HOW it appears, and every offered form (nine-self division, three-head split, nāda-drop, moon-crescent, wheel-unsmeared, power-formed) is negated into higher-ness as pure partlessness — letter and body both fail to divide it. Her plea-praise (grace, cut the doubt; the asked is the essence) turns the doubt itself into the tantra's heart, and Bhairava answers by promising the hidden form while defanging it: unsubstantial as net, dream, mirage-city, and fit only for meditation, not pomp.
sections.RELATED: Hareesh intro post (title gloss, union sense of rudrayāmala); concordance (8 translations) as future witness; Singh outline vv1-7 doubts.

essence: Not nine-self, not word-heap, not three-headed god.
Not nāda-drop, not moon-blockers, not wheel-joined.
Terrors of unawakened minds: mother's sweet for going on.
Free of direction, time, counting; unpointable, untellable.
Inner self-taste joy: Bhairavī's full-formed state.
Stainless world-filling body: who worships, which pleased?
Sung state: she, supreme goddess in supreme form.
Power-powerful non-difference: supreme power of supreme self.
Fire's burning not separate: entry begins it in knowing-being.
Entered power-state, undivided contemplation: Śiva-formed, Śaivī named.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta settling toward śānta (wonder of the unspeakable)
rasa.sthayibhava: vismaya settling into śama (wonder calming into quiescence)
rasa.justification: The denials pile wonder higher — each not-this makes the form stranger — and the passage lands on undivided contemplation and a named mouth, where wonder quiets into statement.

sections.SUMMARY: Every form denied: not nine-self, not word-heap, not three-headed, not nāda-drop, not wheel — free of direction, time and counting, untellable. Her terrors are a mother's sweet for going on. Then the positive: inner self-taste joy, full-formed Bhairavī; stainless world-filling body whose worship becomes the question; sung as supreme goddess, power-and-powerful undivided yielding supreme power; fire's burning only as entry in knowing-being; and the entered state — undivided contemplation, Śiva-formed, mouth called Śaivī.
sections.FUNCTION: Completes the object-question by exhausting forms, then names the form that survives denial.
sections.KEY TERMS: āveśa (possession-sickness — the negated danger); anuttara carried as unpointability; saṃvid (awareness as the only locus); Śaivī (the mouth — speech itself initiated); kṛtrima (made — the contrast with akṛtra elsewhere).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: The mouth named here (Śaivī) makes the coming dialogue itself the practice's vehicle — words as doors.
sections.BOUNDARY: Still no technique; the first breath-practice stands at the next section's threshold.
sections.EXPLANATION: The negation-verse pair works by exhaustion: self-division, word-heap, three-head, nāda-drop, moon-crescent, wheel-course — all pictures, none the thing. The terrors of unawakened readers are confessed as pedagogy (mother's sweet lures the child onward), and the unpointability is stated outright: free of direction, time and count. What survives is not another picture but a state — inner self-taste joy, Bhairavī full-formed — and a mouth: stainless world-filling body raising the worship-question, power-and-powerful as non-difference, fire's heat beginning only in knowing-being, and finally undivided contemplation entering the Śiva-form whose speech is Śaivī.
sections.RELATED: Hareesh upāya note (vv24+ = practices begin); the mouth (mukha) of v20 reappears as the request's door in the next song.

essence: Lamp-ray-sun known so by power Śiva known.
Trident-marked, skull-adorned: void, designation-free.
Full-formed state sought: the means-door begged as known.
Breath above, life below: filling at two arising places.
Wind's sky-pair turning: Bhairavī manifests Bhairava's form.
Blossomed power neither goes nor enters: Bhairava-form by thoughtlessness.
Any breath-phase's end is the calm that shines by power.
Subtler contempler at twelve-end: calming, Bhairava's rise.
Lightning-rise, wheel by wheel to three fists: great rise.
Twelve-letter course through gross-subtle-supreme: freed, Śiva.

rasa.dominant: śānta with vīra undertow (stillness carrying resolve)
rasa.justification: Each prescription is a stilling (fill, contemplate, thoughtlessness, calm) while the optatives keep resolve alive — the rise to Śiva is effort landing in quiet.

sections.SUMMARY: Analogy and denial give way to door: the full-formed state sought, its means begged as known. Then the first body-works: breath meeting at two places; Bhairavī manifesting Bhairava-form through the turning wind; blossomed power needing no going; any breath-phase ending in shining calm; the subtler contemplated at twelve-end rising like lightning wheel by wheel; a twelve-letter course through gross, subtle, supreme — freed at last, Śiva.
sections.FUNCTION: Opens the practice section: door begged, then breath, wind, calm, rise — each stilling prescribed in optative.
sections.KEY TERMS: praveśa (entry as meeting-place); kumbhaka (breath-hold as calm-site); cakraviśrāma (wheel-resting; cf. saktavijnana terms, different system); dvādaśānta (twelve-end — recurring locus); saṃpuṭa (casket image returns later).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Practices here seed every later block: voids (p05), lotus-casket (p08), twelve-end (p10) all return as locations.
sections.BOUNDARY: Outcome statements (Śiva, Bhairava-rise) are promised, not demonstrated — the witnessing verses come later.
sections.EXPLANATION: The door-verse converts years of question into a how: means as known, told as asked. What follows is graduated somatic work — breath filling at its two arising points; the sky-pair's turning making Bhairava's form manifest through Bhairavī; blossomed wind-power refusing motion so Bhairava-form arises from thoughtlessness alone; every breath-phase ending where calm shines by power; the subtler ray contemplated at the twelve-end rising in lightning-steps to the great rise; and the whole body mapped as a twelve-letter course whose completion is freed-Śiva.
sections.RELATED: Hareesh: vv24-27 foundational visarga practice block; Singh kumbhaka notes; twelves recur as a structural number in the body-map.

essence: Filling to crown, brow-toss bridge: thought-free mind goes forth.
Feathers, forms, circles: in unsurpassed void, entry in heart.
Wherever thought: void, wall, supreme, vessel — self dissolved boons.
Mind in skull: from firmness the highest mark is marked.
Lotus-fiber middle channel: god shines through meditated sky.
Hand-blocked gaze, brow-split: drop's middle holds supreme standing.
Fire-tilak drop at heart's dissolution-end: meditating dissolving.
Unstruck, vessel-ear, broken sound: word-brahman bathed, brahman attained.
Prolonged oṃ ends in void-contemplation: to voidness she goes.
A letter's two ends as void: void-formed man becomes.

rasa.dominant: śānta with vīra (stillness with piercing resolve)
rasa.justification: These are the fierce-adjacent practices (piercing, skull, hand-blocked gaze) yet every verse aims at void and calm — vīra serves śānta, never spectacle.

sections.SUMMARY: Esoteric block: mind to crown by quick filling, cross the brow-toss bridge thought-free; aids of feathers, forms, circles give entry in unsuppressed void wherever thought rests; skull-seat for marking the highest from firmness; the lotus-fiber channel shining god through meditated sky; hand-blocked gaze and brow-split finding supreme standing in the drop; the fire-tilak dissolving at heart's end; sounds — unstruck, vessel-ear, broken, river-rushing — bathing into word-brahman; prolonged oṃ pouring toward voidness; and a letter's two ends read as void making void-formed.
sections.FUNCTION: Carries the āṇava-level piercings to their void conclusions — sound and gaze as doors.
sections.KEY TERMS: bhrūkṣepa-setu (brow-toss bridge); tāluka/capala (skull-seat context); dṛg-bādha (hand-blocked gaze); brahmāṇḍa/brahma (word-brahman bathed); praṇava (oṃ as prolonged utterance).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Sound-practice here expands into the music-instrument and letter-practices ahead; void-method connects to p05.
sections.BOUNDARY: No results yet reported — attainment-claims stay in the l08-eve verses beyond.
sections.EXPLANATION: The verse-cluster is a sequence of thresholds: anatomical (crown, brow, skull), objectual (feathers, forms, walls, vessels), sensorial (hand-blocked gaze, drop, tilak), and finally sonic — unstruck, vessel-ear, broken sound, river-rushing all resolving into word-brahman, then into the void that prolonged oṃ pours one into. The letter practice (v40) distills the method to eight syllables: beginning and end contemplated, void through and through — the formless doctrine stated as technique.
sections.RELATED: Hareesh v40 = his Yukti #14 (śāmbhava-upāya) — upāya tags noted as support only; Kṣemarāja on brahman-bathing; āṇava-block per Hareesh (vv31-39 esoteric).

essence: Long tone, undivided mind: supreme-sky body at limit.
Body-mantra's gross course ends moon-drop: void-uttering, Śiva.
Own body as all directions: undirected mind, sky proceeds.
Back, root voids contemplated: body-disregard, void-minded.
Back, root, heart voids steady: thoughtless-rising from thoughtlessness.
Mere moment's voidness: sharing thoughtless nature.
Body-stuff gone, sky-pervaded: contemplation grows steady.
Skin as wall, nothing inside: the unmeditated-sharer.
Lotus-casket mid: undivided, supreme fortune won.
Twelve-end mind-dissolving: the reality-mark firms.

rasa.justification: Ten practices in a row, each producing a quieter noun — sky, Śiva, void-minded, thoughtless, steady, fortune — the song's whole arc is a descent into stillness.

sections.SUMMARY: The void-block: ordered sound seating sky-body at its limit; body-mantra ending in moon-drop void-utterance; own body taken as all directions; back and root voids yielding void-mind, heart-void added for thoughtless-rising; a moment's voidness making one thoughtless in nature; sky-pervasion steadying contemplation; skin read as wall until even the meditated drops; the lotus-casket mid-point winning fortune; and mind's twelve-end dissolving firming the reality-mark.
sections.FUNCTION: Multiplies void-contemplation into a full map of locations — sound, body, wall, lotus, twelve-end.
sections.KEY TERMS: śūnya (void as active, not negation); padma-sampuṭa (lotus-casket); dvādaśānta (twelve-end); nirvikalpa (thoughtless); dravya (body-stuff).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Purifies the field the fire-practices (p06) then pass through; twelve-end reappears at p10.
sections.BOUNDARY: The unmeditated-sharer's status is stated, not explained — no metaphysics added.
sections.EXPLANATION: A cartography of emptiness: the same void seen from ten angles — acoustics (long tone at the perceptual limit), mantra anatomy (gross letters ending in moon-drop), proprioception (all directions as one body), anatomy (back, root, heart), duration (a single moment suffices), wall-illusion (skin dividing inner from nothing), the casket mid-point, and the twelve-end where mind's dissolving writes the reality-mark firm. Each practice both negates a location and claims a steadiness — nothing is left to stand on, and the standing improves.
sections.RELATED: Hareesh central-channel block (vv28-30) precedes; Kṣemarāja on śūnya-methods; same void-word as the oṃ-practice at p04's end.

essence: Mind cast at twelve-end: strangeness drops away in days.
Time-fire burns own city: calm-shining at the end.
Fancy-burned world leaves only man-ness in the non-other mind.
Minutest realities in own body: the supreme is manifested.
Weak power at twelve-range, heart-entered: freedom won.
Ordered world-course run: mind dissolves at its end.
Śiva-reality meditated at world's ends: the great rise.
Universe void-become: mind merged, vessel of merging.
Vessel gaze, wall left: at dissolution, made-of-that.
Mountain-wall gaze: mind dissolved, turning's wasting born.

rasa.dominant: śānta with adbhuta undertow (stillness with the burnt-world wonder)
rasa.justification: The burning, dissolving, voiding verbs are fierce, but each ends in calm-shining, supreme rise, or born-from-waste — destruction staged as quieting, and that inversion is the wonder.

sections.SUMMARY: The burning-and-void block: the mind cast at twelve-end until strangeness wears away in days; time-fire consuming one's own city into calm-shine; fancy's fire leaving only man-ness; minutest realities in own body manifesting the supreme; the weak power entering heart winning freedom; the ordered world-course dissolving mind at its end; Śiva-reality meditated at world-ends raising the great rise; and three vessel-gazes — pot, mountain wall — where dissolution makes made-of-that and births the wasting of turning.
sections.FUNCTION: Turns contemplation into combustion: fire, burning, waste — always ending in what remains after.
sections.KEY TERMS: kālāgni (time-fire); bahirmukha-bhāva (fancy as what burns); svasattā-minutiae (minute realities); tattva-lakṣya (reality-mark); laya (merging as vessel).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Fire and wall-methods feed the wave-practices (p07); the vessel returns in v59 after the interim bliss-block.
sections.BOUNDARY: The burning is internal contemplation, never ritual fire — the verses mark it as fancy's end, not pyre.
sections.EXPLANATION: This cluster converts void into event: time rises from its place and burns the city of self; fancy itself is the fuel whose ash is man-ness; even the minutiæ of reality in one's body become the field where the supreme shows; the weak power, brought to heart at twelve-range, purchases freedom; the ordered world-course runs itself out into mind's dissolution; and at the world's ends, Śiva-reality meditated raises the great rise. The vessel-practices return: gaze in pot or mountain-wall, and once the dividing wall of skin is passed, made-of-that.
sections.RELATED: Fire-practices = classical āṇava-upāya per Hareesh; vessel/wall imagery shares p05's void-map; time-fire echoes Parātriṃśikā's kālāgni usage (distinct work).

essence: Both states, knowing: middle — reality shines forth.
Consciousness restrained: contemplation expands exceedingly.
All-body fancy: undivided mind, supreme rise.
Two winds clashing: evenness-knowing rises, yogin vessel.
Own bliss-filled world remembered: own nectar, supreme bliss.
Application manifests great bliss — reality shines through.
Bound channels, up-breath: happiness spreads at ant's pace.
Mind happiness-cast between fire-poison: yoked by memory-bliss.
Only brahman-reality's happiness, self-told, is told.
Licking, churning, pounding memory: power-absent bliss-flood.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta charged with vīra (wonder armed with intensity)
rasa.justification: The bliss and wind-blocks peak in intensity — clashing winds, nectar, sweet-taste, bliss-flood — yet each is staged as meditative placement (cast, remembered, yoked): wonder the practitioner wields rather than suffers.

sections.SUMMARY: The bliss-block: both states abandoned for the middle where reality shines; restrained consciousness expanding exceedingly; all-body fancy raising supreme rise through undivided mind; the two winds meeting where evenness-knowing makes the yogin into vessel; whole worlds remembered filled with own bliss and nectar; application manifesting great bliss through which reality shines; channels bound so happiness spreads at the ant's slow pace; mind cast happiness-made between fire and poison, yoked by memory-bliss; and the tongue-practices — licking, churning, pounding — carrying memory to bliss-flood even when power is absent.
sections.FUNCTION: Peak-intensity block: bliss as method, sensation as door, memory as the bridge to flood.
sections.KEY TERMS: samādhi (middle-resort as both states left); svānanda/svāmṛta (own bliss and nectar); bharitā-avasthā (filled state); jihvā-dhvani (tongue-practice names); manas-tarpaṇa (memory as yoking).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Bliss-flood flows into the joy-dissolving songs (p08); vessel imagery continues from p05.
sections.BOUNDARY: The taste-practices remain nameless-situated (woman-bliss, mouth) — carried literally, never moralized or bowdlerized (Roche note in lore).
sections.EXPLANATION: Where p03-p06 were anatomy, this is affect: the middle-reality reached by leaving both poles; consciousness so restrained it expands; the yogin made into a vessel at the wind-clash; whole worlds remembered as one's own bliss, own nectar; application—practice—turning technique into manifest great bliss that shines reality through; breath channeled until happiness crawls out at the ant's pace; mind placed between fire and poison and yoked by remembering sweetness; and finally the body's tastes — licking, churning, pounding — becoming doors even when the power itself is absent, so that memory alone floods.
sections.RELATED: Hareesh: vv68-69 powerful sexual experiences as access (his framing); Singh's lehana-note; v70's lehanā read literally per Roche.

essence: Joy risen, dissolved into: of that mind may be.
Eating-drinking joy's bloom: fancy the filled state.
Tasted objects' happiness: absorbed into one-selfness.
Content mind held: supreme-bliss-own-form proceeds.
Sleep's outer range perished: supreme goddess shines.
Dappled sky gaze fixed: own self-form shines.
Skeleton, anger, licking, sky-going: attainment shines.
Asymmetric seat: supreme full mind.
Armpit-sky half-bent arms: calm by dissolving.
Fixed gaze cast down: unsupported mind, Śiva.

rasa.dominant: śānta with vīra undertow (stillness at the edge of intensity)
rasa.justification: Every verse ends a blaze into a still noun — mind, state, selfness, form — the fierce pretexts (skeleton, anger, dark sky) are all converted; the rasa is quiet where the material burns.

sections.SUMMARY: Where bliss dissolves into what remains: meditated joy becoming that mind; eating and drinking's bloom fancyed as the filled state; tasted objects absorbed into one-selfness; content mind held until supreme-bliss-own-form proceeds; sleep's perished outer range as the goddess' shining; gaze fixed in dappled sky showing self-form; the fierce gazes — skeleton, anger, licking, sky-going — all yielding attainment at their time; the asymmetric seat making mind full; half-bent arms in armpit-sky giving calm; and fixed gaze cast down making unsupported mind go to Śiva.
sections.FUNCTION: Converts intensity into positions: every blazing experience is seated, gazed, and stilled.
sections.KEY TERMS: bharitā (filled state); eka-tā (one-selfness); dṛṣṭi (gaze as the operative sense); āsana (seat-variation); svātmarūpa (self-form as what shines).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Sleep-range (v75) sets up the coming sleep-practices; skeleton/sky gaze continue to p09.
sections.BOUNDARY: The fierce gazes are listed, not explained — no taxonomies of fear added.
sections.EXPLANATION: This block is the hinge from bliss to position: joy must dissolve to leave only mind, the filling must be fancyed to become full, other's objects tasted until they are oneself, and contentment held in place until own-form proceeds forth. Then the senses take over as instruments — dappled sky, sleep's edge, and the deliberately fierce images (skeleton, anger, licking) whose point is the conversion: gaze fixed, even there, attainment shines. The body is arranged into asymmetric, half-bent, downward-cast postures, each producing the next stillness: fullness, calm, unsupported mind.
sections.RELATED: Hareesh notes extreme practices (piercing flesh, dark sky) as intensity-doors — same cluster here; Lakshman Joo's practical notes per Singh for postures.

essence: Mid-tongue awareness, h-uttering: dissolves in calm.
Unsupported own-body envisioning: impurity wastes.
Moving-seat calm: divine flood won.
Unbroken sky-gaze: stunned self wins Bhairava-form.
Crown-sky all Bhairava: blaze-reality enters.
Duality-light known: endless-light-bearing form.
Dark night, dark fortnight: contemplating timira, form comes.
Eyes closed, black before: contemplating, made of that.
Any organ's strike or block: nondual void, self shines.
No drop, no emission: lone a rises, knowledge-flood.

rasa.dominant: śānta with adbhuta (stillness startled by its own gates)
rasa.justification: The gates are uncanny — tongue-uttering, closed eyes, dark fortnights, black-before-eyes — each weirdness resolving into calm, form, shining: wonder at how little it takes.

sections.SUMMARY: The gates-block: tongue mid-mouth with the h-utterance dissolving awareness into calm; unsupported body-vision wasting impurity in a moment; the moving seat's calm winning divine flood; unbroken sky-gaze stunning self into Bhairava-form; crown-sky all-Bhairava letting blaze-reality enter; duality-light known as endless-light-bearing; the deliberate darks — bad night, dark fortnight, black before closed eyes — contemplated until timira itself yields the form and made-of-that; an organ struck or blocked opening nondual void where self shines; and the lone a-syllable, no drop no emission, rising into knowledge-flood.
sections.FUNCTION: Catalogues the text's strangest apertures as reliable doors — darkness and organ among them.
sections.KEY TERMS: hoccāra (h-utterance); stabdhātmā (stunned self); timira (darkness contemplation); nāda-bindu (droplet-emission refusal); ekākṣara (lone syllable).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Sound and dark continue into letter-practices (p10); sleep-vision (p08) prefigures nidrā-practices ahead.
sections.BOUNDARY: Counts as doors only — no hierarchy of doors stated; beginners' suitability not yet addressed (that comes with upāya-talk later).
sections.EXPLANATION: An anatomy of apertures: the tongue's middle with a single h becomes a dissolving route; standing unsupported turns one's own body-vision against impurity; a moving seat shakes out divine flood; gaze unbroken across sky stuns the self into form; crown-contemplation admits blaze; duality's light becomes endless-light-bearing once known as such; and the truly odd gates — a bad night, a dark fortnight, blackness before shut eyes — are treated as equal portals, so that even darkness contemplated becomes form. The organ-practice generalizes: any sensory strike, any blocking of it, enters the nondual void where self alone shines.
sections.RELATED: Hareesh: intensity-doors list (dark sky among them); Kṣemarāja on ekākṣara; v90's sudden knowledge-flood echoes p07's flood.

essence: Emission-ending awareness touches eternal brahman.
Sky-formed self, directions uncovered: own form shows.
Pierced limb, awareness yoked: spotless going in Bhairava.
Inner-making not in me: fancies fall by absence.
Māyā deluding: counted realities never stand apart.
Seen desire led to calm: dissolves where it arose.
Desire unarisen: truly He-I, dissolved, that-minded.
Either desire or knowing: undivided mind sees meaning.
Causeless knowing, anyone's nothing: thus becoming Śiva.
No bodily distinction: contemplating all, world-conqueror.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta tipping into śānta (wonder at identity unmade)
rasa.justification: The He-I realization is the text's climactic wonder, but its grammar is subtraction — no inner-making, no separateness, no anyone — so wonder arrives as emptiness being said.

sections.SUMMARY: The letter-to-identity block: emission-ending awareness touching eternal brahman; sky-formed self uncovered by directions showing own form; a limb pierced and yoked to spotless going; the denial that anything inner-making is inside me, letting fancies fall by their own absence; māyä named as delusion counting realities that never stand apart; sudden desire led to calm where it arose; desire unarisen revealing He-I, dissolved, that-minded; mind set undivided in either desire or knowing seeing reality's meaning; knowledge turning causeless, no one's, Śiva; and no bodily distinction anywhere — the contemplating one conquers the world.
sections.FUNCTION: Subtracts every inner stake until the identity statement stands with nothing behind it.
sections.KEY TERMS: jñāna (knowing as causeless); antaḥ-karaṇa-denial (no inner-making); māyā (delusion as counting); He-I (tadāsmi / so'ham as subtraction-result); sarva-deha (bodies as distinction-less).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Identity-claims prepare the passions-neutral block (p11); 'world-conqueror' prefigures the fruit-talk later.
sections.BOUNDARY: No claim that one cannot act: distinction-less bodies still conquer worlds — difference denied, function intact.
sections.EXPLANATION: Vowel-precision (emission-ending awareness) makes contact eternal; then sky and directions; then the somatic puncture (a limb pierced with needle, awareness yoked) yielding spotless going. What follows is pure apophasis: the claim that nothing inner-making is inside — so fancies fall not by attack but by absence; māyā is only the counting that cannot keep realities apart; desire must be led (not killed) to dissolve where it arose, and unrisen desire reveals the He-I. In either desire or knowing, undivided mind sees meaning; knowledge without ground, without owner, IS becoming Śiva — and the bodies, distinction-less in all, are what the contemplating person conquers worlds with.
sections.RELATED: So'ham dialectic (cf. v97 '=B9haṃ' byte); māyā as kalana (counting) matches Parātriṃśikā's counting-verse — cross-reference as parallel, not source.

essence: Passion-range uncaused: reality remains there.
World as net or picture-whirl: seeing all, joy upsurges.
Neither pain nor joy cast: the middle is knowable.
Everywhere-I-am-thus: gaze seeing none else, happy.
Pot-wall contemplation: all-pervading, all-going born.
Grasped-grasping common: yogin's care in relation.
Self in other's body: own-body-regard dissolved, pervasive.
Supportless mind: thoughts not thought, Bhairava in self.
All-knowing, all-doing: he indeed I — Śiva from firmness.
World-plays as waves and flames: Bhairava's manifest only.

rasa.justification: Passions placed in range rather than fought, poles refused, happiness carried as common — each verse subtracts a preference; the last folds all manifestation into wave-and-flame: everything is display already.

sections.SUMMARY: The neutrality-block: within the whole passion-range reality stays uncaused; the world seen as net or picture-whirl makes seeing-all itself joy; neither pain nor joy receives the cast mind — the middle remains knowable; everywhere-I-am-thus with single gaze makes happy; pot and skin-wall contemplations turning all-pervading into all-going; the yogin's distinction as attentive relation to common awareness; self perceived in other's bodies dissolving own-body-regard; supportless mind cancelling thought until Bhairava stands in self; and the lord lit by all knowing, being, pervading — 'he indeed I' from firmness — with all world-plays nothing but waves and flames.
sections.FUNCTION: Neutralizes preference and self-stake — from passions to relations to identity to display.
sections.KEY TERMS: ṣaḍ-viṣaya (six-passion range); samāna-saṃvid (common awareness); svātmaniṣṭhā (yogin's distinction as care); bhairavatva-as-avatāra (world-plays as manifestations).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Identity (v109) is the pivot between the āṇava cluster and the fruit-sealing verses to come.
sections.BOUNDARY: Carefulness (sāvadhānatā) named but not described — one word, left open.
sections.EXPLANATION: The song works by placement rather than renunciation: the six passions are not fought but ranged, the world held as spectacle so that seeing-all is joy, and even pain and joy refused their usual seats so the middle shows. Self-contemplation expands from body to everywhere (pot and skin-walls dissolving), relation becomes the yogin's only distinction — care rather than attainment — other-bodies receive one's own self, and supportless mind cancels volition until 'he indeed I' is a statement made from firmness rather than belief. Wave-and-flame close the list: nothing outside is real, everything only manifest.
sections.RELATED: Hareesh's intensity/access theme as inverse here (this is equanimity-mode); cf. sutasutra citta as mantra — mind-language shared across the canon.

essence: Whirling body ceasing agitation: supreme state born.
Whatever means — power, knowing, mind-dissolve: Bhairava-form.
Eyes unwinkering fixed: freedom born at once.
Ear-contraction, lower gate: meditating enters eternal brahman.
Above pit, undivided mind: dissolving plainly.
Mind nowhere exitable: pervasiveness, Śiva-state wherever.
Eye-road manifests consciousness: cit-dissolving, full-selfness.
Even passions' ends are states where reality fills.
Mind left in seen thing: unsupported lord spreads.
Slow gaze-withdrawal: knowing abiding in void.

rasa.dominant: śānta with vīra (stillness reached through force of attention)
rasa.justification: The whirling and locking verses are the most physical in the text, yet all produce states whose names are calm, waveless, void — effort's whole direction is stillness, and the rasa registers as resolved quiet after motion.

sections.SUMMARY: From whirling to waveless: body's whirling ceasing agitation so the supreme state is born; any means — power, knowing, mind-dissolving — arriving at Bhairava-form; freedom declared born at the instant eyes lock unwinkingly; ear-contraction and lower gate entering eternal brahman; standing above a pit dissolving mind plainly; no exit from pervasiveness — Śiva-state wherever mind goes; every eye-road manifesting consciousness of the pervader until cit-dissolving fills itself; even hunger, fear and battle-ends states where reality fills; the mind left in the seen thing letting unsupported lord spread; and slow gaze-withdrawal abiding knowing in void.
sections.FUNCTION: Contains the freedom-at-a-glance verse and completes the leaving-the-mind practice set.
sections.KEY TERMS: stabdhā-nayana (unwinkering fixity as freedom-site); saṃkarṇa (ear-contraction); vyāpakatva (pervasiveness as no-exit); dṛṣṭi-nivṛtti (gaze-withdrawal); mūrti-tyāga (mind left in the seen).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: v113's at-once freedom answers the frame's how-question; devotion-practices follow (p13).
sections.BOUNDARY: Freedom at a glance is stated as born, not taught — no technique for the lock is supplied here.
sections.EXPLANATION: Motion first: whirling stops and the supreme state is born from the stopping — any of three means arriving at Bhairava-form. Then the text's sharpest promise: eyes fixed unwinkingly, freedom born at once. The somatics of entering follow — ears contracted, lower gate opened, meditating enters eternal brahman; above a pit, undivided mind plainly dissolves; the pervasiveness argument closes exit: Śiva-state is wherever mind goes because nowhere is outside it. Eye-road after eye-road manifests the pervader's consciousness until cit dissolves into full-selfness; the passion-endings become reality-filling states; and the practice series ends in leaving mind in the seen thing and withdrawing the gaze slowly until knowing abides in void.
sections.RELATED: Hareesh: vv24-27 visarga-foundation; this block completes what p03 opened (breath → lock → leave).

essence: Devotion's excess gives mind: contemplating her, Śiva.
Voidness meditated in all things: even knowing calms.
Neither pure nor impure in Śambhu's view: thought-free happy.
Bhairava everywhere in common things: nondual, no beyond.
Enemy same as friend, honor same as dishonor: happy.
Neither hatred nor passion contemplated: brahman glides middle.
Unknowable, ungraspable, void: as Bhairava — awakening rises.
Eternal-supportless-void: mind into skyless enters.
Wherever mind goes, that instant leaving non-standing: waveless.
Fear resounds all in wholeness: Bhairava's word, Śiva.

rasa.justification: Devotion produces the mind but lands in calm; equalities of enemy/friend and pure/impure flatten all reaction; even fear dissolves into word and waveless — every member ends quieter than it starts.

sections.SUMMARY: The equalizing-block: devotion's excess arising as mind to contemplate her — Śaṅkarī's power — then voidness meditated everywhere calming even knowing; pure/impure both refused in Śambhu-view leaving thought-free happiness; Bhairava in every common thing, nothing beyond, nondual going; enemy and friend, honor and dishonor equal under brahma's fullness; hatred and passion not contemplated so brahman glides in the middle; the fourfold ungraspable contemplated as Bhairava awakening at that end; mind entering the skyless from every sky; mind's going met at each instant by leaving non-standing until waveless; and even fear resounding all-in-wholeness as Bhairava's word making Śiva.
sections.FUNCTION: Equalizes opposites and anxiety itself — the method becomes non-reaction, wavelessness, word.
sections.KEY TERMS: bhakti-udreka (devotion-excess); śāṅkarī (her power); pāpa-kṣaya (sin-wasting as inner sacrifice); tulyatā (enemy/friend equality); bhaya (fear as material, not enemy); śabda (Bhairava-word as agent).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Devotion (v121) introduces bhakti as practice-mode; secrecy verses approach at p16.
sections.BOUNDARY: No ethics-list here; equality is stated as effect of fullness, not moral rule.
sections.EXPLANATION: The block opens the devotional turn: mind born from devotion's excess is itself the power to contemplate — and immediately calms in voidness wherever looked for. Purity-polarities collapse in Śambhu-view, so happiness needs no purification; Bhairava becomes ubiquity (common things, no higher beyond), and equality follows from brahma's fullness rather than effort — enemy, friend, honor, dishonor stand alike. Then the two-way subtraction: neither hatred nor passion contemplated means brahman glides precisely in the middle. The fourfold-ungraspable list is contemplation's object, ending in awakening; every sky-region yields; each mental exit is met by leaving non-standing until waveless; and fear, the last obstacle, becomes the material in which Bhairava's word — and hence Śiva — is heard.
sections.RELATED: Pāpa/homa implicit (inner sacrifice); cf. VBT vv157-159 secrecy — the body of what must not be shown; Hareesh closing-verses analysis.

essence: I-mine-conviction: supportless mind into calm.
Word-meditation timed to meaning aims at all-lord.
Net-question from firmness: calm goes.
Self needs neither knowing nor action: world void.
No bondage, no freedom: terrors reflections in water.
Senses left: self-abiding abides in own self.
One-nature lighting all: knowing and known one vision.
Fourfold wasted: Bhairava-form.
Hundred-plus-twelve told in brief: knower-person.
Yoked here: IS Bhairava; speech curser-and-favorer.

rasa.dominant: śānta with vīra undertow (stillness that ends in sovereignty)
rasa.justification: The block is denial-then-claim: no bondage, no freedom, no inner-making — and then the sudden sovereign claim, speech that curses and blesses: quiet resolving into authority, not agitation.

sections.SUMMARY: Conviction completes the earlier denial: I-and-mine emptied, supportless mind falls calm; word-meditation timed to meaning aims at all-lord; the net-question resolved from firmness yields calm; self needing neither knowing nor action makes world void of both; bondage, freedom, terrors all reflections in water; senses left, self-abiding abides; one-nature lighting all gives single vision; the fourfold wasted yields Bhairava-form; a hundred-plus-twelve told in brief makes the knower-person; and yoked here one IS Bhairava whose speech performs curse and favor alike.
sections.FUNCTION: Clears the last metaphysical obstacles, then flips into sovereign identity — quiet as power.
sections.KEY TERMS: pratipatti (conviction as mechanism); śabda-abhyāsa (word-meditation); prati-bimba (reflection-model of bondage); caturka (the fourfold); sāmānya-saṃvid (one-nature lighting).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Closes the teaching-section; the fruit-praise and japa-counts follow (p15).
sections.BOUNDARY: The hundred-plus-twelve count is recension-sensitive (flagged in argmap) — never used to force dhāraṇā numbering.
sections.EXPLANATION: Three sūtra-pairs do final demolition: conviction removes the last holding ('I-mine-this'), word-meditation converts speech into aimed aim at the all-lord, and the net-question dissolves into firmness-given calm. Then the old question of agency returns — self needs no knowing, no action, so world-possessions are void — and bondage, freedom and terrors are all dismissed as reflections (sun in water). With the senses left, only self-abiding remains; one-nature lights knowing and known into a single vision; the fourfold (manas, consciousness, power, self) wasted gives Bhairava-form. The count-vows: hundred-plus-twelve in brief for the knower. And the turn: yoked here, one IS Bhairava — the text's highest authority — whose speech now performs curses and favors without remainder.
sections.RELATED: Count (100+12) vs Hareesh's 116 practice-verses framing — flagged, not reconciled; sovereign-speech = sāmraṭ-bhāva, cf. Śivasūtra sovereignty themes.

essence: Ageless he attains: all-gathering lord of yoginīs.
Freed yet living, unsmeared: supreme great-lord body.
Who mutes, meditates, worships, pleased? Rhetorical.
Outer oblations: procedures in gross things only.
Real japa: self-sound mantra-natured in supreme state.
Meditation unmoving, formless — not bodily imagining.
Worship: firm mind dissolving in undifferentiated sky.
One-yoking day by day: full-formed state, utter fullness.
Void-fire oblation with awareness-ladle.
Sacrifice is contentment: wasting sins, protecting all.

rasa.dominant: vīra with śānta (resolve closing the practice arc)
rasa.justification: Fourteenth-block riddles (who mutes, who worships) strip ritual to inner stances, yet the count-verse and contentment-sacrifice keep a strong volitional edge — resolution without agitation.

sections.SUMMARY: The redefinition-block: agelessness attained as all-gathering yoginīs' lord; freed-yet-living body unsmeared; rhetorical dismantling of outer worship — who, what, how of oblation answered by the inner: japa is self-sound in supreme state, meditation is motionless intellect, worship is firm mind dissolving in sky; day-by-day one-yoking ripens full-formed state; the great void-fire receives the awareness-ladeled oblation; and sacrifice itself becomes contentment, wasting sins and protecting all as effect, not rite.
sections.FUNCTION: Redefines japa, dhyāna, pūjā, homa as inner postures — ritual vocabulary relocated into stillness.
sections.KEY TERMS: sāmānya-japa (self-sound as japa); manonāśa (fourfold wasting); bharitākāratā (full-formed state); cetanā-sruca (awareness-ladle); tṛpti-as-yāga (contentment as sacrifice).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: The who-is-worshipped riddles (v143-144) pave the worship-field verses (p16).
sections.BOUNDARY: Outer procedures are called gross, not forbidden — 'here procedure outer' locates rather than bans (kept argmap-accurate).
sections.EXPLANATION: A catalogue of renamings: bondage and freedom both drop out (v135's reflection-model), then each ritual noun is reissued at inner value — muting becomes self-sound in supreme state, meditation is motionless formless intellect (explicitly NOT bodily imagining), worship is firmness dissolving in sky, oblation is made with the awareness-ladle in void-fire, and the sacrifice is contentment itself, whose by-products are sin-waste and universal protection. Practice day by day in one yoking condenses the whole into full-formed contentment.
